document_title: 664 acres, staked in feet. Taylor's data center terms
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Left in Williamson County, no zoning. Annexed into Taylor, terms in feet.

The city published both sides before the October 8th council vote. The land is 664 acres east of the city limits, for data centers and on-site power.

The proposed terms put data centers, generation and batteries at least 700 feet from the south line near FM 112. The developers would commit $28.2 million to the city, Taylor ISD and nonprofits. They ask for no tax abatement.

The noise term waits on one measurement. Without the agreement the city lists the state's 85 dBA. With it the cap is 65 dBA or the level before construction, whichever is greater. An acoustic study at the property lines would set that level.

The council's regular meetings are in the City Hall Council Chambers.

How loud is the land near FM 112 before anything is built?

S1.headline: Taylor's terms, in feet
S1.body: The City Council votes October 8th on a proposed agreement for a 664-acre data center campus with its own power generation. The stakes in this field mark the south line and the distances its terms set.
strings: The City Council votes October 8th on a proposed agreement for a 664-acre data center campus with its own power generation. The stakes in this field mark the south line and the distances its terms set.

S2.kicker: Without the agreement, the city says
S2.headline: Without it, no zoning at all
S2.body: The developers withdrew their annexation and zoning application on September 3rd. The city says that without the agreement the land stays in unincorporated Williamson County, which has no zoning authority.
strings: Without it, no zoning at all

S3.kicker: The terms, drawn at their distances
S3.headline: From the south line
S3.body: Near FM 112, a buffer of at least 400 feet with earthen berms at least 6 feet high. Accessory structures at least 500 feet back. Data centers, generation and batteries at least 700 feet back.
strings: Near FM 112, a buffer of at least 400 feet with earthen berms at least 6 feet high. Accessory structures at least 500 feet back. Data centers, generation and batteries at least 700 feet back.
The terms, drawn at their distances

S4.kicker: Noise, as the terms write it
S4.headline: 65 decibels, or the level before
S4.body: The terms cap the campus's noise at 65 dBA or the level before construction, whichever is greater. A study at the property lines would set that level. Without the agreement, the city lists the state's 85 dBA.
strings: The terms cap the campus's noise at 65 dBA or the level before construction, whichever is greater. A study at the property lines would set that level. Without the agreement, the city lists the state's 85 dBA.

S5.kicker: The hall is drawn for scale
S5.headline: The closest a data hall gets to the south line
S5.body: Data centers, power generation and battery storage would stand at least 700 feet from the south line. The hall here is drawn for scale, and the size of the real buildings is not in the record.
strings: The closest a data hall gets to the south line

S6.kicker: The berm as described, not built
S6.headline: 6 feet of earth
S6.body: A buffer of at least 400 feet along the south line would carry landscaping and earthen berms at least 6 feet high. The city says the buffer areas would separate the development from nearby homes.
strings: A buffer of at least 400 feet along the south line would carry landscaping and earthen berms at least 6 feet high. The city says the buffer areas would separate the development from nearby homes.

S7.kicker: The first fill, drawn as one basin
S7.headline: 1.575 million gallons to start
S7.body: Cooling would run in a closed loop on reclaimed water with an initial fill of 1.575 million gallons, drawn here as one basin 6 feet deep. Drinking water would stay out of cooling except in three circumstances.
strings: Cooling would run in a closed loop on reclaimed water with an initial fill of 1.575 million gallons, drawn here as one basin 6 feet deep. Drinking water would stay out of cooling except in three circumstances.

S8.headline: About 1,400 signed a ban petition
S8.body: In June residents petitioned for a temporary ban on new data centers. KEYE reports the city found it can't go on the ballot. Texas Standard reports coalition members filed a motion with the Third Court of Appeals.
strings: In June residents petitioned for a temporary ban on new data centers. KEYE reports the city found it can't go on the ballot. Texas Standard reports coalition members filed a motion with the Third Court of Appeals.

S9.headline: The vote is October 8th
S9.body: Big Watt Digital and PowerHouse Data Centers would commit $28.2 million and ask for no tax abatement. Regular council meetings are held in the City Hall Council Chambers.
